outcome: No result settling this exact question was found. The one 2024-2026 item that surfaces in every search (Väänänen's July 2025 arXiv survey 'Interpolation in model theory') discusses a related but distinct fact: the 'Beth-closure' of the logic L(Q≤2ωcof) is compact and has the Beth property, but it explicitly does NOT satisfy Δ-interpolation (which the survey identifies as the same thing as Souslin-Kleene interpolation) — the opposite of what this bullet's hypothetical logic would need. That construction is also not new; it is attributed (via reference [50] in the survey) to earlier work, not to the 2025 paper itself.
summary: This bullet asks whether there is a logic L with the Beth property AND Δ-interpolation, that is compact, but lacks the (Craig) interpolation property. This is a fine-grained question in abstract model theory sitting at the intersection of the Beth property, Δ-interpolation (equivalently Souslin-Kleene interpolation), compactness, and full interpolation — a hierarchy where interpolation ⇒ Δ-interpolation ⇒ Beth ⇒ weak Beth. The triage pass flagged Jouko Väänänen's July 2025 arXiv survey 'Interpolation in model theory' (2507.19097) as a possible hit, and I fetched both the abstract and the HTML full text to check it directly. The survey does discuss a closely related construction: the 'Beth-closure' of the generalized-quantifier logic L(Q≤2ωcof) is compact and has the Beth property, but the survey states plainly that this Beth-closure logic does NOT satisfy interpolation, 'not even Souslin-Kleene interpolation' — and the survey treats Souslin-Kleene interpolation as synonymous with Δ-interpolation. That is nearly the reverse of the bullet's question: the bullet wants a logic that DOES satisfy Δ-interpolation (in addition to Beth and compactness) while still lacking full interpolation, whereas the Beth-closure example is a logic that fails even Δ-interpolation. So this construction does not answer the stated bullet; it is a different (already-known, cited to reference [50], i.e. pre-existing) counterexample answering a nearby but distinct question. I could not find any paper, survey, or announcement dated after 26 January 2024 that constructs or refutes the existence of a logic satisfying Beth + Δ-interpolation + compactness while lacking interpolation. The survey's own explicit open-problem list (e.g. 'Is there any proper extension of first order logic that is (countably) compact and has the interpolation property?', 'Are FO quantifiers the only generalized quantifiers giving a regular logic with Craig interpolation?', open questions about Shelah's logic and about a logic between L(Qωcof) and L(aa) with Craig interpolation) does not include this exact question, and does not flag it as newly resolved or newly open. Given the depth and age of this sub-area (Makowsky, Shelah, Stavi, Barwise-Feferman era work from the late 1970s-1980s), and that the 2025 survey — clearly written to catalogue exactly this kind of question — does not present this bullet as settled, I am reasonably confident this remains open. No AI system of any kind is mentioned in connection with any of the material found; this is traditional pen-and-paper mathematical logic.
competing_reading: One could argue the Beth-closure construction is 'close enough' to count as addressing the bullet, since it shows the same rough phenomenon (Beth + compact + not-full-interpolation) in a logic that is 'almost' Δ-interpolation-adjacent. But the bullet's wording specifically requires Δ-interpolation to HOLD, and the survey states it explicitly fails for this example, so by the letter of the question this is not a match, and I classified it as no_change_found rather than partial or progress. If a reader disagreed and felt any discussion of this exact quartet of properties, even a negative example, constitutes 'progress' in mapping the landscape, they might record 'progress' instead of 'open' — but no bound, case, or new example was actually established in the window that moves the stated existence question either way.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that either (a) exhibits a logic satisfying Beth + Δ-interpolation + compactness but lacking full interpolation, thereby answering the question affirmatively, or (b) proves no such logic can exist (a negative resolution), or (c) an updated edition/erratum of Barwise-Feferman or a survey explicitly stating this specific combination has been settled with a citation and date.
